Subject: Brightly pilot — budget and per-model volume split (recap & next steps)

Hi Aditi / Luke —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a short set of asks so we can put together the pilot proposal and conservative vs. aggressive cost scenarios.

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Initial launch: 5M tokens / month (production-facing NLP features) with user growth to ~25M tokens / month over 12 months.
- Feature mix: conversational chat for customer-facing flows (approx. 60% of tokens), embeddings for semantic search and personalization (approx. 25%), and a small rerank/selection step (approx. 15%).
- Budget guidance: internal target is roughly $400–$550 per 1M tokens on average (goal: keep pilot unit economics near that range).

Preliminary unit-costs (Redwood options attached, see redwood_cost_options_v2.pdf):
- Chat model (chat-legacy-v3 / quantized variant): ~$650 per 1M tokens
- Embeddings (text-embed-3 small): ~$120 per 1M tokens
- Rerank (rerank-light-v1): ~$300 per 1M tokens

Weighted example: 60% chat, 25% embed, 15% rerank => (0.6*650)+(0.25*120)+(0.15*300) = ~$465 per 1M tokens (pilot baseline).

Asks / next steps (please reply inline):
1) Confirm the monthly starting volume (is 5M tokens/month the right conservative kickoff number?)
2) Confirm the model mix split (60/25/15 or should we shift more to embeddings initially?)
3) Tell us whether you need: cost-only estimate OR cost + reserved capacity pricing (reserved commitment reduces unit cost by ~15–30% depending on term).
4) Any procurement constraints or timing for PO/contract sign-off (important for quoting reserved capacity).

I'll produce two cost scenarios once you confirm (conservative = starting volumes; aggressive = 12-month growth ramp). Attaching Brightly_RFP_QnA.xlsx with our notes and a draft pilot scope (pilot_scope_v1.docx).

Cheers,
Sergio

Subject: Re: Brightly pilot — budget and per-model volume split (recap & next steps)

Thanks, Sergio — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Starting volume: yes, conservative kickoff should assume 5M tokens/month. We expect a steady ramp to ~18–25M tokens/month by month 12 depending on adoption; please include a 3-point ramp (month 1/6/12).
- Model mix: 60% chat is our best guess, but the first 2 months may skew heavier on embeddings as we index and iterate on search/recommendation rules. Please include an alternate split for first 60 days: 45% chat / 40% embeddings / 15% rerank.
- Procurement: procurement wants a simple two-line proposal: a) 90-day pilot (metered) and b) optional 12-month reserved capacity (commit + discount). We'll need a line-item for estimated $/1M tokens and a monthly projected spend for the pilot (so they can route budget).
- Compliance: we will need SOC2 report and evidence of data retention/audit logs (happy to collect the list but please attach the compliance packet).

Can you provide two cost tables: conservative (5M start) and aggressive (ramp to 25M), and a blended $/1M for each? Also an example monthly spend for months 1, 6, 12 (using both the normal and reserved pricing).

Appreciate it — we want to share this with procurement tomorrow morning PST.

Best,
Aditi Shah
Head of Product
Brightly

Hi Aditi —

Quick note from pricing ops: we can produce the two tables Aditi requests and will include both metered pilot pricing and a reserved capacity option. A few specifics to confirm on your end to make the tables tight:

- Expected average prompt + response length for chat (tokens per request): tiny (avg ~120 tokens) vs. medium (~450 tokens) has large impact on $/1M. Do you have a sample or estimate?
- Embedding batch size: are embeddings batched offline (large batches) or on-demand per request? Batched jobs will lower per-unit cost.

We can model two scenarios:
A) Conservative: 5M tokens/mo start; initial split 60/25/15; conservative token lengths (chat avg 200 tokens)
B) Aggressive: ramp to 25M tokens/mo; initial 45/40/15 for first 2 months, then 60/25/15; chat avg 300 tokens as users engage more.

I'll attach a versioned cost options PDF (redwood_cost_options_v2.pdf) with examples showing the 15%–30% unit-cost improvement under 12-month reserved pricing. If you want, we can also include a one-off pilot credit to offset initial engineering time (we typically propose $5k–$15k in credits depending on scope).

Camila
